claims.text: The proposed approach integrates atomic-level disorder-aware phonon-scattering models with machine-learning techniques.
The integrated approach will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEA compositions more accurately than traditional effective-medium approximations.
The target materials are single-phase, compositionally homogeneous HEAs with randomized distributions of constituent elements.
The disorder-aware simulations account for atomic-mass variance and interatomic-force-constant fluctuations.
The machine-learning component is trained using both simulated and experimental thermal-conductivity data.
Atomic-level chemical disorder enhances phonon scattering through variations in atomic mass and local bonding environments.
Chemical disorder is inherent in the HEAs covered by the hypothesis.
Higher atomic-mass variance is associated with lower phonon thermal conductivity through increased phonon scattering.

Within the designed single-phase HEA domain, the integrated approach will reduce thermal-conductivity prediction error by approximately 30% relative to effective-medium or simpler machine-learning methods.
Current effective-medium and conventional machine-learning models typically have thermal-conductivity prediction discrepancies exceeding 30% for disordered multielement systems.
The approach is expected to be applicable only to single-phase HEAs in which chemical disorder is the dominant phonon-scattering mechanism.
Significant secondary-phase segregation can cause the approach to produce inaccurate predictions.
Extrinsic microstructural defects can cause the approach to produce inaccurate predictions.
Restricting measurements to phase-pure samples is intended to avoid confounding from grain boundaries and secondary phases.
The exact quantitative improvement cannot be established until high-throughput experimental validation is performed across a broad range of HEA compositions.
Failure to achieve at least a 30% reduction in prediction error relative to conventional models within the single-phase HEA domain would falsify the hypothesis.
